idiom_name: key class with a qualified-private constructor (private[Owner]) nested in the authorised object
implementation_notes: Scala's qualified private is the grant: private[C] makes a member accessible only from code inside the class C and its companion module, where C must denote an enclosing class or package (Scala 2.13 specification, classes and objects). The passkey therefore becomes a key class whose constructor is private[Owner] and which is nested in the authorised object - the constructor stays out of everyone else's reach while the key type itself remains visible in the restricted signature. A package qualifier (private[pkg]) scales the same construct to a whole package; plain private is not enough, because a nested class's private constructor is not accessible to the enclosing class.
pitfalls: private[Owner] requires Owner to enclose the declaration; a sibling object or a type declared later in the same file will not compile as the qualifier.
Package-qualified private grants every file in the package, and packages are open to new files - the grant is as stable as the package contents.
Case classes synthesise public apply/copy; a key must be a plain class with an explicit qualified-private constructor.
